<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Mālatīmādhava is a Sanskrit play written by the ancient Indian poet Bhavabhūti. It tells the story of the love affair between Mālatī, the daughter of a minister, and Mādhava, the son of a wealthy merchant. The play is divided into ten acts, each of which explores a different aspect of the relationship between Mālatī and Mādhava. The plot revolves around the challenges the lovers face in their quest to be together, including the disapproval of Mālatī's father and the machinations of a jealous rival suitor. The play is notable for its use of poetic language and its exploration of themes such as love, jealousy, and fate.</div></div></div>

<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">is unique in its portrayal of the love story between the two main characters, Mālatī and Mādhava, as it focuses on their emotional and psychological journey rather than physical aspects of their relationship. The play also incorporates elements of both Sanskrit drama and poetry, with the use of various musical instruments and songs, making it a unique and complex work of art. Additionally, it explores themes of love, devotion, sacrifice, and karma, presenting a nuanced and multi-layered exploration of human emotions and relationships.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature as it is considered one of the earliest plays in Sanskrit, and the first romantic play. The work is also notable for its portrayal of the love story between Mālatī and Mādhava, which is presented in a nuanced and complex manner. The play's use of various literary devices, such as vivid imagery and intricate wordplay, further demonstrates its literary importance. Additionally, the play's influence can be seen in later works of Sanskrit literature, particularly in the genre of romantic plays. Overall, Mālatīmādhava holds a special place in the canon of Sanskrit literature, and its significance continues to be recognized by scholars and readers alike.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-quotations">Quotable Quotations</button></h2><div id="work-acc-quotations" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">1\. ये न््म ्े मचददह नः प्रथयनतय्वज््ं ज्नगनर रे प््मपि र्न् प्रपर ननष यतनः । उतितसयरेऽससर ्म्म ्ोऽपि स्म्न््म्गा ््लो ह्ययं पनर्वम्र्ववििुल् च िृथ्वी ॥ \[्म्लरी्म्््व्म् – १.६\] ye nāma kecidiha naḥ prathayantyavajñāṃ jānanti te kimapi tān prati naiṣa yatnaḥ | utpatsyate'sti mama ko'pi samānadharmā kālo hyayaṃ niravadhirvipulā ca pṛthvī ||</div></div></div>
